title: Arc: send opum-agent the per-repo Story file lists, resolved on origin/dev
summary: Owed to the orchestrator before it routes per-repo Arc records. Working-tree counts already sent are NOT usable for this.
description:
opum-agent asked for exact per-repo file lists before routing an Arc record into each repository's own tracker. This is that deliverable, filed as a task because ten accumulated handoffs here left owed items as prose and prose is not closeable.

WHY IT CANNOT REUSE THE NUMBERS ALREADY SENT. The counts this session produced (lore-web 3, quest-web 3, opum-web 0, opum-marketplace 0, opum-fleet 1, plus lore-cli 23 raw) were measured on WORKING TREES, whole-repo, including fixtures and .repro-scratch. OPAG-277's own counts were measured on each repo's origin/dev. Different objects, and this repo already carries that caveat on LCLI-552. A file LIST handed to another repository for action must be resolved on origin/dev by ref, never from a sibling's checkout -- a sibling working tree is mid-task on some branch and is not its repository.

METHOD: for each of the ten fleet repos, `git ls-tree -r origin/<default> --name-only` filtered to *.md, then read frontmatter for an exact `type: Story` match. Do NOT use a bare recursive grep in this repo's harness: grep here is ugrep and -r silently skips gitignored files, which would under-report. Report the count READ alongside the count FOUND so an empty result cannot read as a clean one.

SCOPE NOTE: the lists are a deliverable to opum-agent, not authority over those repositories. Each repo files and executes its own record (OPAG-277's scope ruling; Mechanism C, OPAG-244).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every fleet repo resolved by ref on its own origin/dev, never from a sibling working tree
Each list states the number of files READ as well as the number matched
lore-cli's own list distinguishes the 12 real docs from the raw match count, as LCLI-552 already records
Sent to opum-agent with the resolution basis named, so the working-tree caveat does not travel with it
